title: Section rhythm
rule: Use one project spacing scale and preserve a clear large-to-small hierarchy: section gap > component gap > inline gap. Do not invent a new spacing scale for one section.
check: Compare desktop and mobile section rhythm against adjacent sections and existing global spacing tokens.

title: Container ownership
rule: If the same width problem appears across multiple areas, fix the established global container token/owner; keep page CSS for page-only exceptions.
check: Verify no horizontal overflow and compare at least one unrelated page before changing a global container value.

title: Responsive reflow
rule: Prefer reflow, wrapping and fluid sizing over fixed widths. Preserve content order and avoid hiding important content merely to make a breakpoint fit.
check: Check narrow mobile, tablet and desktop widths for overflow, clipped text and broken alignment.

title: Readable type hierarchy
rule: Reuse the project type scale. Body copy should remain comfortably readable; headings should differ by hierarchy, not by arbitrary boldness or many one-off sizes.
check: Verify heading/body contrast, line length, wrapping and consistency with neighboring components.

title: Semantic color reuse
rule: Use existing semantic color tokens before adding raw component colors. New tokens need a repeated semantic role, not a single visual occurrence.
check: Compare hover/focus/disabled states and ensure the change does not create a second near-duplicate project color.

title: Card content hierarchy
rule: Keep one dominant visual, one primary text hierarchy and one clear action. Avoid equal visual weight for image, badges, metadata and CTA.
check: Scan the card at thumbnail size: image, title and primary action should remain immediately distinguishable.

title: Stable product image area
rule: Use a stable media box and object-fit behavior so mixed source images do not change card height or distort products.
check: Test portrait, square and landscape product images in the same grid row.

title: Testimonial trust hierarchy
rule: Prioritize quote readability and credible attribution. Decorative rating/avatar elements should support, not overpower, the customer statement.
check: Verify long quotes do not create unstable card heights and attribution remains readable on mobile.

title: Hero focal hierarchy
rule: Give the hero one focal message and one primary action; visual media should reinforce the message without forcing text into unstable overlays.
check: Verify the focal order still works when the image crops at mobile width and when slide content changes.

title: Button hierarchy
rule: Use one clear primary action style and quieter secondary actions. Keep sizing, radius and icon alignment consistent with the existing component system.
check: Verify hover, focus and disabled states and ensure nearby secondary actions do not visually compete with the primary action.

title: Form clarity
rule: Keep visible field meaning, clear focus state and error feedback near the affected field. Placeholder text should not be the only label for important inputs.
check: Keyboard through the form, trigger an error and confirm the field remains identifiable after text is entered.

title: Icon consistency
rule: Use the icon system already loaded by the project/Builder for functional icons. Match stroke/fill style and size; reserve standalone SVG/media assets for brand marks or unique logos.
check: Verify the icon source is actually loaded, alignment matches text, and icon-only controls have an accessible name.

title: Visible keyboard focus
rule: Interactive controls need a visible focus treatment that is not removed merely for visual cleanliness.
check: Navigate the touched UI using only the keyboard and confirm focus remains visible and ordered logically.

title: Readable contrast
rule: Muted styling must remain readable. Do not solve hierarchy by pushing important text into low-contrast gray-on-gray combinations.
check: Check normal, hover and disabled states against their actual backgrounds, not isolated color swatches.

title: Purposeful motion
rule: Use motion to explain state or continuity, not as decoration on every element. Prefer transform/opacity for simple transitions and preserve reduced-motion behavior when motion is substantial.
check: Rapidly trigger the interaction twice and confirm the final visual and semantic state stays correct.

title: Navigation density
rule: Keep primary navigation scannable and predictable. Secondary utilities should not visually compete with the main navigation or force cramped labels.
check: Verify long labels, active state, dropdown alignment and mobile navigation without horizontal compression.

title: Intentional image crop
rule: Do not stretch source media to satisfy layout. Define the display ratio separately and choose contain/cover according to whether preserving the whole subject or filling the frame matters more.
check: Compare source dimensions with rendered dimensions and verify the important subject remains visible at mobile crop.

title: Shared component consistency
rule: When the same component appears in multiple places, update its established shared renderer/style owner instead of cloning a visually similar local version.
check: Inspect at least one second usage of the shared component and confirm the change is intended there too.
